Classification guard: the single authored edge asserts association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly:true). It records that hypotension is documented among the risk factors for non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy and that dialysis-associated ischaemic optic neuropathy is attributed to intradialytic hypotension, not that hypotension caused visual impairment in any individual; the located evidence is a small dialysis case series plus a narrative review, the target disease is multifactorial, and an individual claim therefore requires blood-pressure records with dates, ophthalmic documentation of the optic neuropathy, chronology, and exclusion of the competing optic neuropathies listed on the edge.

Duplicate-scope guard: the visual-impairment identity already receives ten windows (pituitary-neoplasm, ptosis, retinal-dystrophy, cataracts, aphakia, chalazion, corneal-scarring, glaucoma, hydrocephalus, hypertensive-retinopathy), none of which is a hypotensive-hypoperfusion window - the batch-46 hypertensive-retinopathy window shares the target but runs in the opposite exposure direction through hypertensive microvascular injury, whereas this window is hypoperfusion of the optic nerve head; no dizziness, syncope, falls, or orthostatic edge is authored because the orthostatic-specific literature belongs to the catalogue's distinct orthostatic-hypotension identity, which is queued to author its own symptomatic windows, and vasovagal-syncope owns the reflex mechanism (parallel-pathway, entity-specificity, and direction-inversion guards).
governanceNotes: D1 batch 47 (2026-09-24): one bounded association edge authored - hypotension to visual-impairment (rank 1), ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, and mechanismCategory MICROVASCULAR_METABOLIC (hypoperfusion of the optic nerve head). The proposition rests on the Donaldson 2022 case series and review of dialysis-associated non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy, which describes the condition as secondary to intradialytic hypotension, reports three cases with catastrophic visual consequences and recurrence in the same eye, and links it to the intradialytic blood-pressure fall, and on the Desai 2005 review of non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy, which lists nocturnal hypotension alongside hypertension and diabetes among the risk factors for a disorder presenting as sudden painless loss of vision. The edge is not raised to causation: the condition-specific evidence is a three-patient dialysis series, the review-level evidence lists hypotension among several coexisting vascular risk factors of the same disorder, the underlying disease is multifactorial with a structural predisposition (small cup-to-disc ratio), and arteritic, embolic, diabetic, and compressive optic neuropathies are competing explanations that the located evidence does not exclude.

Counter-evidence and scope screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) shared exposure - the same review lists hypertension and diabetes among the risk factors for non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy, so the hypotensive window does not displace the hypertensive or diabetic microvascular pathways and is not asserted as the dominant mechanism; (ii) population specificity - the case series concerns haemodialysis patients, in whom fluid and electrolyte shifts, anaemia, and uraemia also act on optic nerve perfusion, so the hypotension-specific contribution is not separable in that series and the broader review is used to bound the proposition; (iii) nocturnal dipping - the review's reference to nocturnal hypotension is recorded as the proposed ambulatory exposure, which is why blood-pressure documentation must include night-time or ambulatory measurement rather than clinic readings alone.

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) no dizziness, falls, or syncope edge - no catalog identity exists for falls or syncope outside vasovagal-syncope, the located dizziness and syncope literature is orthostatic-hypotension-specific and the catalogue carries a distinct orthostatic-hypotension identity queued to author those windows (parallel-pathway and entity-specificity guards), and a hypotension-to-vasovagal-syncope edge would invert the direction because the reflex causes the blood-pressure fall (direction-inversion guard); (ii) no chronic-kidney-disease, stroke, or cognitive-disorder edge - the located hypotension-centred evidence concerns optic nerve perfusion, and chronic hypoperfusion encephalopathy and ischaemic-organ windows either belong to their own primaries or lack condition-specific data (intermediate-chain and zero-record guards); (iii) no optic-atrophy edge - atrophy is the late sequela and the located sources document acute ischaemic optic neuropathy with acuity and field loss rather than progression to atrophy with denominators (target-specificity guard); (iv) no blindness edge - the case series documents catastrophic visual loss but not incident blindness incidence, and the blindness identity receives no current incoming window (zero-record guard); (v) no seizure, coma, or delirium edge - no catalog identity for coma or delirium and no condition-specific hypotensive seizure data were located (wrong-target and zero-record guards); (vi) duplicate-scope note: this batch adds the first hypotension-primary window to the registry.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Clinical literature documents ischaemic optic neuropathy in the setting of low blood pressure: the Donaldson 2022 case series and review of dialysis-associated non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy states that the condition occurs secondary to intradialytic hypotension, presents three cases with catastrophic visual consequences and recurrence in the same eye, and relates them to the intradialytic blood-pressure fall, and the Desai 2005 review lists nocturnal hypotension together with hypertension and diabetes among the risk factors for a disorder whose presentation is sudden painless loss of vision - a reproducible co-occurrence association rather than an individual causal nexus.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established: the condition-specific evidence is a three-patient haemodialysis series in which fluid shifts, anaemia, and uraemia are not separable from the hypotensive episode, the review-level evidence lists hypotension among several coexisting vascular risk factors for a multifactorial optic neuropathy with a structural predisposition, and no incident cohort relates blood-pressure levels to subsequent visual loss; an individual determination therefore requires blood-pressure records including ambulatory or nocturnal measurements with dates, ophthalmologic documentation of the optic neuropathy and its acuity and field deficits, temporal proximity of the visual loss to the hypotensive episodes, and exclusion of the competing optic neuropathies listed on this edge.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized microvascular route is described: the optic nerve head is supplied by the short posterior ciliary arteries whose perfusion depends on an adequate mean arterial pressure, so a sustained or nocturnal fall in blood pressure can reduce perfusion to a watershed region with limited autoregulation and produce ischaemic injury and axonal swelling, which degrades central acuity and the visual field - the sequence described in the Donaldson 2022 account of dialysis-associated ischaemic optic neuropathy secondary to intradialytic hypotension and reflected in the Desai 2005 review's listing of nocturnal hypotension among the risk factors; the case-series design, the multifactorial target disease, and the competing causes leave individual attribution hypothesized.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Nocturnal blood-pressure dipping reduces optic nerve head perfusion during sleep when autoregulation is already challenged, and in dialysis patients rapid fluid removal, anaemia, and uraemia add independent ischaemic stress, which is why the located series cannot attribute the visual loss to hypotension alone.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association only: a three-patient dialysis case series attributes ischaemic optic neuropathy to intradialytic hypotension and a narrative review lists nocturnal hypotension among the risk factors for the same multifactorial disorder, but there is no incident cohort linking blood pressure to visual outcomes and the coexisting hypertension, diabetes, structural disc predisposition, and dialysis-related factors are not separable, so no at-least-as-likely-as-not probability is asserted and an individual claim requires blood-pressure documentation with chronology, ophthalmic characterization of the optic neuropathy, and exclusion of competing optic neuropathies.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Blood-pressure records with dates and values, including ambulatory or nocturnal measurements where obtained and any documented hypotensive episodes (intradialytic, postural, or medication-related); ophthalmic documentation of the optic neuropathy (disc appearance, visual acuity and visual-field testing, optical coherence tomography where performed) with dates; the chronology of the visual loss relative to the hypotensive episodes and to any dialysis sessions; evaluation for competing optic neuropathies including giant-cell arteritis, diabetic papillopathy, optic neuritis, embolic retinal or ophthalmic artery occlusion, compressive lesions, and glaucomatous or inherited optic atrophy; assessment of anaemia, renal function, and cardiovascular status; ophthalmology or neuro-ophthalmology assessment of whether the hypotensive history materially contributed to the visual impairment
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy from giant-cell arteritis
Hypertensive or diabetic microvascular optic neuropathy and diabetic papillopathy
Embolic or thrombotic retinal and ophthalmic artery occlusion
Compressive, glaucomatous, or inherited optic atrophy and other structural optic neuropathies

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: a case series and review of dialysis-associated non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy states that the condition occurs secondary to intradialytic hypotension and reports three cases with catastrophic visual consequences, and a narrative review lists nocturnal hypotension among the risk factors for a disorder presenting as sudden painless visual loss, establishing a reproducible co-occurrence association; the edge is not raised to causation because the condition-specific evidence is a three-patient dialysis series in which fluid shifts, anaemia, and uraemia are not separable, the target disease is multifactorial with coexisting hypertensive and diabetic risk factors, and no incident cohort links blood pressure to visual outcomes, so the consensus remains NOT_ESTABLISHED with blood-pressure documentation, ophthalmic characterization, chronology, and competing-cause requirements and no probability estimate is asserted.
